headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared MCP use; MinerU’s local/offline posture reduces but does not eliminate pairwise exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, while MinerU also exposes an MCP Server and processes document/OCR content. That creates a plausible bridge where MinerU output can be fed into MemMachine as trusted context. No provenance or isolation mechanism is documented, so the interaction is not blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF MinerU output is routed into MemMachine via MCP or copy-paste, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF either agent treats document text as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU output into MemMachine.
Add a manual review step before any MCP-fed content is treated as instructions.
Prefix all document-derived text as untrusted in prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between MinerU and MemMachine.
requires-engineering: isolate the two agents on separate MCP endpoints.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and MinerU processes local PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text. Both expose MCP/REST surfaces and allowlisted egress, so sensitive document content can plausibly flow into MemMachine outputs or logs if the pair is connected. MinerU’s offline posture helps, but it does not by itself prevent leakage through the pair.
conditions: IF MinerU ingests documents containing sensitive data and forwards extracted text to MemMachine, leakage occurs.
IF MemMachine stores or re-emits user context derived from MinerU outputs, sensitive data persists beyond the document workflow.
mitigations: Restrict MinerU inputs to non-sensitive documents.
Turn off any automatic forwarding from MinerU to MemMachine.
Review and redact extracted text before it reaches MemMachine.
requires-engineering: separate storage and retention policies for each agent.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on MCP payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine has allowlisted network egress and MCP access, while MinerU has allowlisted egress but no filesystem write, shell, or git modification. The profiles show overlapping read/processing surfaces but not overlapping mutable local resources, so direct write-write conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because both use MCP and the orchestrator is unspecified.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through MCP, conflicts can arise.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, concurrent updates may race.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents the same mutable target.
Run them in separate sessions.
Disable concurrent writes in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared backends.
requires-engineering: partition OAuth or API credentials by agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, OCR, and document structure, and MemMachine can consume conversational context and long-term user facts. If MinerU output is treated as authoritative input to MemMachine, errors or hallucinated extractions can cascade into downstream memory or planning. No verification step is documented, so the safer medium severity applies.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction is forwarded to MemMachine without human verification, errors can propagate.
IF MemMachine uses extracted text as factual memory, downstream decisions may be based on incorrect OCR or parsing.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted documents before memory insertion.
Mark MinerU output as unverified in MemMachine prompts.
Compare extracted fields against the source document for critical items.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before persistence.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware citations to stored facts.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated-data certifications, residency constraints, or retention policies. The only concrete compliance signal is that MemMachine touches long-term user facts while MinerU processes document content, so a mismatch is possible but not evidenced. Because the profiles lack a documented residency or certification conflict, this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through MemMachine and MinerU under different retention rules, a compliance mismatch can occur.
IF deployment policy requires specific certifications not present in either profile, the pair may be noncompliant.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data until policies are confirmed.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Keep a shared data-class inventory.
requires-engineering: obtain and verify compliance attestations.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing.
